description: Weekly plan for ages seven to twelve: prayer out of love, managing anger, study, screens, sleep, worry and siblings.

topics.focus: Prayer out of love, not obligation

actions.text: Pray one prayer a day together at home, and let them call the adhan if they like.
Use a simple chart they tick after each prayer, and praise consistency rather than perfection.
Remind them gently, in one word, at the adhan — no threats, no punishment.
Ask: "What makes prayer hard for you?" and listen to the answer before giving advice.

topics.focus: Managing anger: tools for child and parent

actions.text: Agree on a "calm corner" they go to when angry, then talk once they have calmed down.
Teach simple steps for anger: stop, take three breaths, then speak.
Talk about your own anger calmly in front of them: "I'm angry, and I'll calm down first."
Praise them when they put their anger into words instead of shouting or hitting.
Fix a quiet time and place for study every day, away from screens.
Split study into short blocks with breaks in between.
Praise effort and persistence, not just the grade.
Ask about a subject they enjoy and let them teach you something from it.
Write a simple screen agreement together: when, how long and where.
Keep devices out of bedrooms at night, for the whole family.
Play their favourite game with them once this week and ask what they like about it.
Suggest a fun alternative for free time: sport, reading or something with their hands.
Keep a fixed bedtime on school days and don't push it much later at weekends.
Turn screens off an hour before bed and keep the phone outside the room.
Cut down on sugar and stimulants in the evening.
Make the last minutes of the day a quiet talk and the bedtime adhkar together.

topics.focus: Worry and fear: listen and reassure

actions.text: Set aside a quiet time for them to tell you what worries them, without interrupting or teasing.
Teach slow breathing: breathe in counting to four, breathe out counting to four.
Face the fear together in small, gradual steps, and praise every step.
If the worry lasts for weeks and affects sleep or school, consult a specialist.
Give each child some one-to-one time this week, even if it is short.
Avoid comparing siblings' grades or behaviour.
Give them a shared job at home and praise how they work together.
When they fight, hear each one out separately before you decide.

worship.text: Pray Maghrib or Isha together at home on four days this week.
Read one page of the Qur'an together after one prayer each day.
Choose a small good deed together this week: feeding someone, helping a neighbour, or charity.
Sit together for a few minutes after Maghrib for the evening adhkar.
Visit a relative or someone who is ill together this week.
